newsitem.title: CHINA: Listed firms to obey rules-China securities chief.
newsitem.headline: Listed firms to obey rules-China securities chief.

text.p: China's newly listed firms must standardise their operations, must not buy and sell their company shares and must use funds raised in accordance with the public offer statement, China's securities chief said.

In remarks published in the China Securities newspaper on Thursday, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, Zhou Daojiong, said the securities watchdog would continue to crack down on and punish offenders strictly.
He listed five points that should be strictly followed by firms listed since 1996, including a ban on buying and selling of their own company shares.

These firms must release information only according to the law, must perfect the legal person system, must use funds raised in accordance with public offer and rights issue statements and those that invest in high-risk industries must strengthen policy supervision and risk management, he said in the remarks made last weekend in Guangdong.
Whether the listed companies obeyed the rules would affect not only the healthy development of the firms themselves but also the future of the stock markets, Zhou said.

He urged a change of ideas, stressing that directors must be responsible to all shareholders and must have the concept that the board of directors and managers must have their specific functions and responsibilities.
